annotationRationale: The main subject is length geometry in a regular hexagon. Center-based right triangles and congruent vertex triangles provide distinct routes; their Pythagorean and cosine-law concepts remain in the respective method mappings.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is correct. No area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Independently, the center-to-vertex distance is 2 and the center-to-side-midpoint distance is √3. The four requested sides consequently have length √7, giving perimeter 4√7, choice D. The stem, choices, and key agree. No current question figure is supplied, but the verbal specification is sufficient.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: No shared-question methods were supplied. AoPS Solution 1 is retained as center geometry; Solutions 2 and 4 are merged into the cosine-law route. LIVE's coordinates and AoPS Solution 3 compute the same perpendicular components as the center route, so a separate coordinate method is unnecessary. AoPS Solution 5's answer-choice bounds are omitted reasonably: for this short problem they require an additional obtuse-triangle bound while yielding only choice elimination. The two retained methods independently determine the exact perimeter.
review.annotationCheck: cnm_266 is a precise assessed concept for the primary center-based method, and midpoint lengths are appropriate support. Pythagoras and the distinct vertex-angle/SAS/cosine-law concepts are correctly retained in their respective method mappings.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is correct. No area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Equal radii and 60-degree central angles produce equilateral triangles of side 2. The midpoint altitude has length √3, and the stated 30-degree plus 60-degree angle establishes perpendicularity. Opposite vertices and opposite midpoints produce four right triangles with the same legs, proving perimeter 4√7.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: AoPS Solution 1 is the correct source for this exact center-and-Pythagoras route. The candidate adds explicit angle and perpendicularity reasoning in original prose. Third-party provenance is correctly represented by source-informed-original; no shared-bank provenance applies.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The first move is motivated by the equilateral subdivision. Radius, apothem, perpendicularity, and equality of the four lengths are explained sufficiently to reconstruct the argument without a diagram.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_266 directly covers central angles, radii, and apothems; cnm_174 covers both right-triangle calculations; cnm_055 covers the midpoint length. All immediate nodes are precise and supported.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Each listed triangle has sides 1 and 2 enclosing a 120-degree angle, so SAS establishes the four requested lengths are equal. The cosine-law calculation gives 1+4−4(−1/2)=7, hence the perimeter is 4√7.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: AoPS Solutions 2 and 4 support the claimed vertex-triangle route. The candidate independently states and correctly applies the general cosine formula, avoiding the missing factor in the displayed formula of supplied Solution 4. The third-party credit and source-informed-original basis are accurate.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening identifies the common triangle structure. The interior-angle calculation, included-angle justification, SAS correspondence, cosine formula, and trigonometric value are all explained at use.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: Polygon angle sums, midpoint lengths, SAS, trigonometric reduction, and general cosine-law application all occur explicitly. The general cosine-law node correctly covers the negative cosine used here.
